newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds no EU guarantee for back interest on benefits.
newsitem.headline: Court finds no EU guarantee for back interest on benefits.

text.p: The European Court of Justice told a British citizen that although no basis in EU law exists to receive interest on past due social security benefits, a claim for member state liability may be pursued.
Eunice Sutton sought back interest on "invalid care allowance" payments granted by the Social Security Commissioner in Britain.

Sutton was denied the back interest in the British court because under British law, "no interest is payable on arrears of social security...prior to the decision of the competent body in favour of the claimant," the court said.

The court found that article 6 of the EU directive, which requires states to adopt measures to assure benefits to persons previously discriminated against, did not include the payment of interest on arrears of benefits to be an essential component of the right conferred.

Sutton argued that the Francovich ruling in the European court entitled her to compensation for loss suffered as a result of the UK's failure to fully implement the directive guaranteeing equal treatment for men and women in social security matters.

The court told Sutton that if she could meet the test of Francovich, i.e., prove an individual right was seriously breached by Britain's failure to fully implement a directive and that she sustained damage as a result of that breach, the national court could assess her claim for back interest as damages.
Reference from the High Court of Justice, Queen's Bench Division, England and Wales
The Queen and The Secretary of State for Social Security, ex parte Eunice Sutton

on the interpretation of Community law in regard to the right to obtain interest on arrears of a social security benefit falling with the scope of Council directive 79/7/EEC on the progressive implementation of the principle of equal treamtent for men and women in matters of social security (OJ 1979 L 6, p 24)

Article 6 of Council directive 79/7/EEC on the progressive implementation of the principle of equal treamtent for men and women in matters of social security does not require that an individual should be able to obtain interest on arrears of a social security benefit such as the invalid care allowance, when the delay in payment of the benefit is the result of discrimination prohibited by directive 79/7. However, a member state is required to make reparation for the loss and damage caused to an individual as a result of the breach of Community law. Where the conditions for state liability are fulfilled, it is for the naitonal court to apply that principle.
